sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup, paths and reason for generating
sections.what: Explains in its header why the types are generated rather than written by hand, and how to run it with or without check mode. Sets the paths to the schema and the output file, and loads the conversion tool.
sections.why: The header states the reason: a hand-written copy would drift from the schema without any test noticing.
sections.watch_out: The paths are relative to this file's location, so moving the script makes it fail to find the schema.

sections.name: fingerprint (part 1)
sections.title: Fingerprinting the schema and generating types
sections.what: Makes a short fingerprint of the schema file's exact bytes, converts the schema into TypeScript code with fixed style options, and makes a second fingerprint of that generated code.
sections.why: The comments say any byte change to the schema is a real change, including reworded descriptions, so raw bytes are hashed; the second fingerprint catches hand edits to the output.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint of the generated code depends on exact formatting, so changing the conversion options changes every fingerprint.

sections.name: fingerprint (part 2)
sections.title: Stale check and writing the types file
sections.what: In check mode, compares the file on disk with a freshly generated version and exits with failure if they differ, explaining whether the schema moved or the file was edited. Otherwise it creates the folder if needed and writes the new types file.
sections.why: The comments say two causes need two messages, because printing the same hash under the word stale would look like a bug in the checker.
sections.watch_out: The check reads the committed fingerprint with a fixed text pattern, so changing the header wording would stop the cause message from working.

summary: Creates TypeScript type definitions for the process record from the shared JSON schema, and can check that the saved file still matches what the generator would produce.
purpose: Keeps the frontend's record types in step with the schema defined from the Python models, so the two cannot quietly drift apart.
why: The header says a hand-written copy would drift from the schema silently, and that the Python tests and the JSON check cannot see a TypeScript file that has stopped matching.
how: Reads the schema file and computes a short fingerprint of its raw bytes. Converts the schema into TypeScript code with fixed style options. Computes a second fingerprint of that generated code and writes a header containing both fingerprints above it. In check mode, it compares the full result with the file on disk and exits with failure if they differ, explaining whether the schema moved or the file was edited.
inputs: The schema file under the packages folder. An optional check flag switches the script into check mode.
outputs: The types file at frontend/src/types/process-record.ts, containing a header and the generated types. In check mode it prints an up-to-date message or a stale message with both fingerprints and a cause, and exits with 0 or 1.
risks: The fingerprints depend on the exact bytes the Python exporter writes, so a formatting change in the exporter makes every check fail. Running without check mode overwrites the types file without asking. The header says do not edit, but nothing stops an edit; only the checks catch it.
debug: If the check reports a mismatch, compare the committed fingerprint with the schema fingerprint printed beside it. If they differ, the schema moved, so regenerate. If they match, the file was edited by hand or the generator changed, so regenerate and review the difference. If the types file is missing, run the generate command in the frontend folder.
